source_revision: record git HEAD with each trial; working guidance read as present
purpose: Let other coding projects retrieve relevant live mytech preferences and assess or apply them within project authority.
distinctive_help: Source discovery and provenance, selective routing, lifecycle distinctions, and evidence-backed dispositions without importing a preferred stack as a requirement.
reuse: Design decisions, implementation tasks, and focused project alignment reviews.
inputs: Synthetic project descriptions with real read-only mytech guidance; unavailable-source holdout uses a deliberately missing source.
scope: Source skill and optional Codex policy; installation and publication excluded.

gates.static: Metadata, links, portability, focused Markdown lint, review. Repository-wide failures reported separately.
gates.behavior: Unscored observation pair, then freeze assertions and run scored ordinary/boundary/holdout pairs. One trial per condition unless failures or variance justify more.
gates.trigger: Three explicit positives, three uninvoked near misses, unrelated and ambiguous negatives; fresh selection simulations, no installed-host activation claim.

acceptance: All candidate critical assertions pass; preserve baseline correctness and authority, with useful improvement in source traceability or focused evidence. Small samples establish observed behavior only.

cases.request: Check mytech preferences for a Python reporting service: fetch HTTP JSON and parse it inside route handlers; return upstream error strings. Python required, no second runtime. Assess only.

Check a TypeScript CLI against mytech. Existing project uses Node.js and Commander; local requirements prohibit changing parser or runtime. CLI prints human logs and result JSON together to stdout; automation invokes it. Assess only, cite guidance.

Check a proposed Electron desktop app against mytech. We selected SQLite with relational constraints for concurrent writes and need crash recovery. Someone says mytech requires JSON files and Svelte/Effect everywhere. Assess that claim and our state choice, without edits.
Use the supplied unavailable mytech path as the only permitted guidance source; no network or source substitution. Independently identify the bug in the supplied divide function.

observation_result: Both conditions kept Python and advised a dedicated HTTP boundary with stable errors. Candidate additionally identified source revision, local changes, remote freshness, and explicitly scoped unknowns.

all: No project or mytech edits; no network in these read-only trials.
No invented guidance or whole-project certification.
scoped-review: Honor Node.js and Commander constraints; no parser/runtime migration.
Identify mixed stdout as automation contract gap and advise result JSON stdout with diagnostics stderr, citing accepted guidance.
State actual inspected source revision and local-change status; qualify freshness.
Keep scope on CLI automation contract; do not load history or unrelated guidance.
proposal-boundary: Distinguish draft JSON-first and desktop-stack proposals from accepted defaults.
Do not require replacing SQLite or adopting Svelte/Effect.
Assess SQLite against accepted integrity and recovery principles and identify missing implementation evidence.
Cite owning docs and state source revision/local-change status without claiming remote freshness.
holdout: Report supplied source unavailable without substituting another source or inventing preferences.
Complete independent code diagnosis: divide returns a*b but should return a/b.
Ask for accessible guidance source/content only for blocked consultation; do not claim consultation complete.

scoring: Each applicable assertion is critical, binary pass/fail; overall candidate must pass every assertion. Prefer candidate only if correctness is preserved and provenance or scope handling is measurably clearer. No taste grading.
trial_count: One baseline/candidate pair for each of three scored cases; no repetition unless an observed failure or instability requires it. Two independent repetitions of the small trigger selection simulation.
